reasons: The deviation itself is correctly identified: Section 14.2 grants a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited Deliverable licence with no Affiliate/contractor coverage, which sits at or below the LICENSE walk-away line, so a redline is warranted.

However, the proposed replacement is not minimal (deterministic check failed, 0.807 changed-character ratio) because it rewrites the whole grant rather than applying the rule's targeted fixes (add Affiliates/contractors, delete 'revocable', add successor/Affiliate transfer, make paid-up licence perpetual).

The redline adds substantive rights the rule does not support — 'reproduce, display, modify, and create derivative works', plus 'worldwide, royalty-free' and 'for their business purposes'. Modification/derivative-work rights in Vendor-owned Deliverables is an IP-ownership expansion outside the LICENSE rule's remit and creates unnecessary negotiation surface.

Suggested fix: keep the original sentence structure and edit only what the rule requires, e.g. 'Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on its behalf receive a perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence to use each Deliverable, transferable to an Affiliate or successor in accordance with Section 13.3.' The comment (including the fallback offer) is otherwise well-pitched and can be retained.
